description: Blood-caster - pays for every spell out of its own veins and takes it back with interest.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from data/reference/coa/bloodmage.json (38 real CoA Sanguine talents, role DPS, 'Warlock + Death Knight'). Replaces a 23-node tree with 2 procs and 19 bare numbers. Bloodmage measures second-worst in the game after Witch Hunter. CoA's Thirst is Frontier's VITALITY resource - Bloodmoon Blast generates it, Vampiric Fang spends 30 - and six CoA talents that scale off the live Thirst count are flattened, because nothing in this engine reads a resource amount into a stat or an effect. Stated per node.

nodes.name: Atherann's Wickedness
nodes.description: Increases your Shadow spell damage by up to 9% and your chance to hit by up to 6%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your Shadow damage dealt by 4% and increases your hit chance by 3%.' Authored as the full-investment ceiling at one rank and left to the rank policy.

nodes.name: Cunning of Atherann
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by 24% of your Stamina and 24% of your Spirit.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 20 Passive. Increases your spell damage by 25% of your Stamina and Spirit.' Both pairings are live - spell_power is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS, stamina and spirit are sources. This is what makes a Bloodmage want Stamina on a caster: the class pays for spells with health, so toughness IS damage.

nodes.name: Darkfallen's Embrace
nodes.description: Increases your haste by up to 6%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your spell haste by 3% and increases the range of your Sanguine spells and Bloodbolt by 5 yds.' Range means nothing here.

nodes.name: Blood Banquet
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Valanar's Vengeance and Taldaram's Torment by up to 15%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the damage of Valanar's Vengeance and Taldaram's Torment by 15%.' Already a scalar in CoA.

nodes.name: Night Feast
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Bloodbolt by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each point of Rage now increases the damage of Bloodbolt by 1%, but its Rage cost is increased by 10.' Scaling off the live Rage total is not reachable - get_talent_effects() has no access to a resource amount - so this is a flat bonus at roughly what 40 banked Rage would have given. THE DRAWBACK IS DROPPED: a cost INCREASE has to be written as a negative _cost, which is indistinguishable from the sign error the audit flags, so this node is strictly better than CoA's. Flagged rather than pocketed quietly.

nodes.name: Swarm of Flies
nodes.description: Bloodbolt renews Taldaram's Torment on the target, burning it for 4 more turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your Bloodbolt now refreshes the duration of Taldaram's Torment.' Re-applying the dot IS refreshing it - StatusEffect refreshes on a matching effect_id rather than stacking - so this ports almost exactly. The effect_id is suffixed _talent to keep it distinct from the ability's own application, which carries its own potency. Was dot_duration_pct +6%, which extends every dot rather than refreshing this one.

nodes.name: Hematoma
nodes.description: Bloodbolt heals you for 20% of the damage it deals.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim over 2 ranks: 'Your Bloodbolt now heals for an additional 20% of the damage dealt.' leech_pct without smart:true heals the carrier, which is what this wants - with it, the heal would go to the worst-off ALLY instead. Bloodbolt costs health, so this is the node that makes the spec's filler sustainable.

nodes.name: The Cup Runneth Over
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Bloodmoon Blast, Taldaram's Torment and Bloodbolt by 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the spell power scaling of Bloodmoon Blast, Taldaram's Torment and Bloodbolt by 20%.' There is no key for how much an ability scales with spell power - the coefficients live on the abilities - so it is expressed as damage, which is what the scaling buys.

nodes.name: Blood Parasites
nodes.description: Taldaram's Torment returns 8 Rage and makes the target easier to critically hit.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Taldaram's Torment now generates 3 additional Rage per tick and increases spell critical strike chance against the target by 3% for 15 sec.' PER TICK is not reachable - there is no periodic trigger in this engine - so the Rage lands once on the cast at roughly what three ticks would have paid. 'Crit chance AGAINST the target' has no recipient-side key either; crit lives on the attacker, so it becomes spell damage taken, which delivers the same thing the talent is for. 15 sec is 5 turns.

nodes.name: Blood Prince's Command
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Bloodbolt by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Bloodbolt is now guaranteed to critically strike on enemies affected by Taldaram's Torment.' No effect key reads whether the target carries a debuff, so the condition is dropped - and shipped as a large bonus rather than an unconditional ability_*_crit of 100.0, which is what the literal reading would be and would be a permanent guaranteed crit on the filler.

nodes.name: Twisted Magic
nodes.description: Your critical strikes make the target take 2% more shadow damage per stack for 4 turns, stacking 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your direct harmful critical strikes increase the target's Shadow damage taken from you by 2%, stacking up to 5 times, for 12 sec.' Ports almost exactly - CoA's 2%, 5 stacks and 12 sec (4 turns). The 'from you' part is lost: the debuff raises shadow damage from any source, since a recipient-side key cannot name who applied it. <school>_damage_taken_pct is built by interpolation in Character.take_damage, so shadow is live, and in a status effect it takes percentage POINTS.

nodes.name: Lifedrinker
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Vampiric Fang by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim. Vampiric Fang is the Thirst dump, so this and Dominion of Blood below are the two nodes that make spending Vitality worth banking it.

nodes.name: Dominion of Blood
nodes.description: Vampiric Fang heals you for 27% more.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your Vampiric Fang now heals you for an additional 50% of the damage dealt.' ability_*_healing is the key a heal reads - abilities.py accepts both _healing and _damage on a heal, but _healing is the name that belongs there, and for a long time only _damage was looked up, which silently broke every talent authored the correct way. Was healing_done +3%, which raises every heal in the spec rather than this one.

nodes.name: Bloodsores
nodes.description: Your damage-over-time spells raise bloodsores, increasing your damage by 3% per stack for 3 turns, stacking 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 30 Passive. Periodic damage dealt now has a 20% chance to apply a Bloodsore to your target for 8 sec, stacking 5 times. Bloodsore: Increases the damage of your next Sanguine Rupture and Bloodmoon Blast against the target by 10%.' Two forced changes. It triggers on the dot's CAST rather than on each tick, because no periodic trigger exists, which is why the chance is 100% rather than CoA's 20% - once per cast instead of a roll per tick. And the payoff is a self buff rather than a target debuff naming two abilities, because ability_*_damage cannot be reached from a status effect. CoA's 5 stacks kept; 3% per stack lands on 15%, close to CoA's 10% per stack applying to two spells.

nodes.name: Enthraller
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Valanar's Vengeance and Keleseth's Calamity by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim. ability_*_crit is a PERCENT - the previous tree had 2.0 per rank over 5 ranks, which is CoA's number by a different route but spread so thin that no single point mattered.

nodes.name: Malediction
nodes.description: Malediction leaves the target taking 20% more spell damage for 4 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Condemn an enemy, dealing Shadow damage over 12 sec and increasing the damage they take from your next 5 direct damage spells by 20%.' The 'next 5 spells' counter is not a shape effects have - they expire on turns, not on uses - so it is a 4-turn window instead, which is about how long five casts take. CoA's 20% kept.

nodes.name: Agonizing Pain
nodes.description: Atherann's Anguish leaves the target bleeding for 4 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Damage dealt by your Atherann's Anguish now causes enemies hit to bleed, dealing Shadow damage over 10 seconds.' 10 sec is 4 turns. A proc-applied dot takes a flat potency. Was dot_damage +4%, a general scalar on a node whose whole point is adding a second dot.

nodes.name: Essence Harvester
nodes.description: Taking a heavy blow resets Vampiric Fang and floods you with 20 Rage and 20 Vitality.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Being struck by an enemy while below 35% health instantly resets the cooldown of your Vampiric Fang and grants you Wretched. Can only occur once per minute. Wretched: Generates 10 Rage and 1 stack of Thirst every 1 sec for 10 sec.' No proc payload reads the carrier's own health threshold, so the below-35% gate becomes a 15% chance with a 6-turn internal cooldown - roughly CoA's once-a-minute. Wretched's per-second ramp collapses into one grant, and it is VITALITY because that is what Thirst is here. grant_resource takes one resource, so the Rage half of Wretched is the part that did not fit; Vitality is the one that matters, since it is what Vampiric Fang spends and this node has just reset it.

nodes.name: Cardiac Arrest
nodes.description: Valanar's Vengeance bleeds the target for 4 turns and heals you for a third of its damage.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your Valanar's Vengeance now deals an additional 50% of its initial damage dealt over 10 seconds, healing you for 50% of the damage dealt.' Both halves built off one trigger. The dot takes a flat potency rather than 50% of the hit, since apply_effect cannot size itself from the triggering amount - leech_pct beside it CAN, which is why the heal is a true percentage and the dot is not. Cut to 33% because the dot's flat value lands high at this tier.

nodes.name: Blood Craving
nodes.description: Your damage-over-time spells return 10 Rage.
nodes._source: CoA: '3 min cooldown. You crave blood for 12 sec, for the duration you cannot be interrupted or silenced, and you regain 5% of your maximum health and 15% of your missing Rage every 2 sec.' Frontier has a bloodmage_blood_craving ability already, so this node is not its unlock - no Bloodmage ability carries requires_talent. Built as the sustained version of the Rage half, which is what the spec actually needs: its spells cost health and its Rage abilities are the cheap ones. Interrupt immunity has no key.

nodes.name: Fearmonger
nodes.description: Increases the damage your damage-over-time spells deal by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the tick rate and cost of Taldaram's Torment by 30%.' Ticks are per-turn here, so there is no sub-turn rate to raise - a faster tick rate in real time is simply more damage, which is what this grants. The cost increase is dropped for the sign reason recorded on Night Feast.

nodes.name: Dark Presence
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases spell haste of all party and raid members by 3%. Does not stack with similar effects. In addition, increases your spell haste by 3%.' A talent effect applies to its own character and there is no aura mechanism, so the description says 'your' rather than promising the party a buff it will not receive.

nodes.name: Cursed Ground
nodes.description: Sanguine Rupture splashes 35% of its damage onto up to 5 enemies and leaves them bleeding out.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the cast time of Sanguine Rupture by 2 sec, but now when you strike at least 5 enemies it causes them to bleed out, dealing additional Shadow damage over 2 seconds.' The 5-enemy THRESHOLD is not buildable - nothing counts how many targets a cast hit - so it fires always and spreads to five, which is the same shape pointed the other way. The cast-time drawback has nothing to apply to, so this node is better than CoA's; flagged. Also carries Bloodwell Eruption's crit half, whose radius increase is positional.

nodes.name: Torture
nodes.description: Vampiric Fang heals you for 27% more and steals 20% of the damage it deals.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the leech of Vampiric Feast by 50%. Consuming at least 9 stacks of Thirst with Vampiric Fang now extends the duration of Transgression by 5 sec.' The Thirst-threshold half is the sixth and last of this tree's stack-count nodes and is dropped for the same reason: nothing reads a live resource amount. Vampiric Feast does not exist in Frontier; Vampiric Fang is the ability it describes, so the leech lands there.

nodes.name: Reckless Abandon
nodes.description: Increases your spell critical strike chance by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 40 Passive. Each stack of Thirst now increases your critical strike chance by 1%.' Thirst caps at 10 stacks, so a full bank is 10% - granted flat, because nothing reads a live resource amount into a stat. This is the clearest of the six: CoA's version rewards holding Thirst and this one does not care, which removes a real decision from the rotation. Noted rather than papered over.

nodes.name: Blood Lord
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by up to 9%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Grants your Bloodsore a 15% chance to provide its benefits without being consumed.' Bloodsores in this tree are a self buff that is never consumed in the first place (see that node - the consume needed a target debuff naming two abilities), so there is nothing for this to not-consume. Rebuilt as flat spell damage, which is what a non-consumed Bloodsore was worth.

nodes.name: Vampyr Lord
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Keleseth's Calamity by 18%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage dealt by your Animated Blood by 35%.' ANIMATED BLOOD DOES NOT EXIST in Frontier - three CoA talents name it and the class has no such ability, so there is nothing to scale and ability_bloodmage_animated_blood_damage would have been a key naming no real ability, which audit_talents now catches. CoA's number re-pointed at Keleseth's Calamity, the other area nuke this tree already modifies.

nodes.name: Crimson Terror
nodes.description: Your spell damage rises by half your Spirit, and your critical strikes drink deep - healing you for a fifth of the damage dealt.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Transgression now grants spell damage equal to 50% of your Spirit for the duration.' Transgression's own CoA description in this export is a broken template reference ($6a), so there is no window to tie this to and the conversion is permanent. Paired with a crit leech so the capstone closes the loop the whole spec is built on - every spell here costs health, and this is the node that finally pays it all back. Spirit is a conversion source and spell_power a target, so the first half is live as written.
